deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It contains no formulas, derivations or computations. It is the title and short preface ('Vorbemerkung') of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Über die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe'. He submitted it in Göttingen in 1854, and Dedekind published it posthumously in Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 13 (1867). This manuscript is evidently a fair copy of that text.

The preface makes three statements.
(1) The essay has two essentially different parts.
(2) The first part is a history of research and opinions on 'arbitrary (graphically given) functions' and whether trigonometric series can represent them. In compiling it, Riemann says he was allowed to use some hints ('Winke') from 'the famous mathematician to whom one owes the first thorough work on this subject'. This is Dirichlet, whose 1829 Crelle paper is the reference. The previous page (table of contents) confirms this with '§3 Seit Dirichlet… Erledigung der Frage durch Dirichlet … 1829'.
(3) The second part investigates representability by a trigonometric series 'which also covers the cases not yet settled'. These are functions not satisfying Dirichlet's conditions, for example functions with infinitely many maxima and minima or infinitely many discontinuities. For this purpose Riemann had first to give a short essay on the concept of a definite integral and the extent of its validity. That essay is §§4–6, which contain the definition of what is now called the Riemann integral and its integrability criterion.

The table of contents on the previous page maps out the structure:
- §§1–3: history.
- §§4–6: the integral.
- §§7–13: the investigation proper. This covers series with coefficients tending to zero, the Riemann localization principle, and the 'second' Riemann function F obtained by integrating twice.

The next page begins §1 with the general series a_1 sin x + a_2 sin 2x + … and ½b_0 + b_1 cos x + …, and with the vibrating-string controversy of 1753.

results.what: Programmatic announcement of the structure of the Habilitationsschrift: a history of the representation problem, then a definition of the definite integral, then an investigation of representability by trigonometric series without special assumptions on the function.
results.modern_name: Preface to Riemann's 1854 Habilitationsschrift (origin of the Riemann integral, Riemann's localization principle, Riemann's theory of trigonometric series)

results.what: Acknowledgement of hints from Dirichlet ('the famous mathematician to whom one owes the first thorough work on this subject') for the historical part.
results.modern_name: Riemann's acknowledgement of Dirichlet (Dirichlet 1829 convergence theorem for Fourier series)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the verbatim preface of Riemann's well-known Habilitationsschrift, published in 1867 and widely studied. The page contains no mathematics, and everything on it is already attributed to Riemann.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription is essentially correct and matches the published 1867 text.
'willkührlichen' is Riemann's period spelling and is correctly read. The published text normalizes it to 'willkürlichen'.
The final word reads 'voraufzuschicken' in the manuscript, which fits the image. The published edition prints 'vorauszuschicken'.
The '4' at the right margin is the folio/page number, not part of the text.
The faint mirror-image text visible on the left is bleed-through from the facing page and is not content of folio 4r.
